question: Can each unchanged C004 selected-checkpoint validator obey its per-call, validation-reserve and global GPU limits even when execution stops reaching internal budget checks?
hypothesis: External CPU supervision can stop only the owned validation child at a fixed deadline and preserve honest result/accounting state. This does not guarantee that an uninterruptible kernel process can be terminated or diagnose prior GPU hangs.

sources.consequence: A wait timeout does not terminate the child. Use bounded identity-checked TERM/KILL and file-backed output, and confirm terminal state before closing resource intervals.
A fixed monotonic deadline bounds each selected-checkpoint call despite wall-clock changes; current ledger remainder can shorten but never extend it.
Admit and close under the existing shared ledger lock; reject an already-open GPU interval and count nested wrapper/child time once.

sources.sections: Asynchronous execution and implicit synchronization on CPU/GPU copies
sources.consequence: Python checks between operations cannot bound a blocked synchronization. Use an external CPU supervisor without changing synchronization mode, precision or scientific code.
Respect C004 half-hour per selected checkpoint inside the existing8-hour validation reserve and global48-hour allowance; do not charge B/C or enlarge any allowance.
Reuse exact hash-bound A016 identity, bounded wait and stop helpers; inherit their CPU test coverage without claiming GPU-stall recovery.

differences: Operational wrapper only around already-approved C004; no new samples, model updates, calibration, tolerance/precision/backend changes or scientific criteria. C005v1 live training and v2 future training wrapper remain untouched. Current C004 checks its half-hour/global limits inside the process; C007 enforces those plus the shared validation reserve externally.
contrary_evidence: OS-level uninterruptible processes can outlive TERM/KILL; never claim termination or close their intervals without proof. A stopped diagnostic may lack a raw result or complete check set and cannot be interpreted as a model-quality negative. CPU fixtures cannot certify real GPU recovery.

Retain partial raw artifacts; separate technical_blocked/budget_incomplete from measured numerical outcomes.

protocol.reviews: Each actual C004 scientific result and C007 operational result needs its own literature review before cache or another dependent stage. No automatic review/successor; no retry on failure without substantive review.

success: All scoped CPU checks pass, actual parent/source/consultation guards hold, and later actual operations are bounded or explicitly preserve unconfirmed termination and open accounting. This creates no trained-model validity or performance claim.
stop: Refuse stale/missing lineage, active GPU/trainer or exhausted allocation. On deadline terminate only verified owned child; unconfirmed termination is a technical block with ledger open. Preserve every partial result. Do not alter the live C005 trainer or scientific C004 code.
